2. The petitioner took treatment at Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Byrasandra, by spending Rs.1 Lakh.
As on the date of the accident, petitioner being aged about 58 years, used to earn Rs.30,000/- per month by driving autorickshaw.
Regarding the accident, Wilson Garden Traffic police registered a case in Cr.No.25/2021.

3. In response to the notice, the respondents No.1 & 2 appeared through their respective Advocates and filed separate written statements denying the allegation regarding reason and mode of accident,
nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

4. On the basis of the pleadings on 18.05.2022 this Authority has framed the following issues:-
1. Whether the petitioner proves that due to rash and negligent driving of Mahindra Supro Maxi Truck motor bearing No.KA-51-AF-8110 by its driver dashed to the petitioner who was driving auto rickshaw bearing registration No.KA-01-D- 8582 and he sustained injuries in the accident that occurred on 26.03.2021 ?
2.Whether the respondent No.2 prove that the accident has occurred due to the negligent act on the part of the petitioner himself ?
3. Whether the petitioner proves that Mahindra Supro Maxi Truck motor bearing reg. No.KA-51- AF-8110 is insured with 1st respondent Insurance Company ?
4.Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom ?
5.
What order ?
5. On 07.12.2022, 23.02.2023, 25.09.2023 petitioner deposed as PW.1 and produced 16 documents at Exs.P.1 to P.16.
On 21.07.2024 and 11.08.2024 petitioner produced the evidence of Dr. Chidanand as PW.2 and produced 2 documents at Exs.P.17 & P.18.
On 03.01.2023 respondent No.2-Hemanth Kumar deposed as RW.1 in part and then failed to lead further evidence.
6. I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of the petitioner, respondent No.1 and perused the records.

7. On the basis of the materials placed on record, my findings on the above issues are as under:

 REASONS 8. Issue Nos.1 & 2 :- In the evidence petitioner has stated that on 26.03.2021 at about 9 a.m., when driving autorickshaw bearing No.KA-01-D-8582 on Wilson Garden main road from Agadi Hospital towards Shanthi Nagar bus stop, driver of a Mahindra Truck bearing No.KA-51-AF- 8110 drove the same negligently from Wilson Garden 4 th cross, dashed the same to the rear part of the autorickshaw, thereby caused accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.

9. In the written statement, respondents No.1 and 2 denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of accident and asserted that due to the sole negligent driving of the autorickshaw by the petitioner, the accident taken place.
10. In the cross-examination PW.1 stated that he was driving the autorickshaw towards Shanthinagar on the left side of the road, he was turning the autorickshaw from left side to right side.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that as he made an attempt to turn the autorickshaw in the place where there was no turning, met with an accident.
PW.1 admitted that in Ex.P.3-sketch, it is noted that the accident taken place in the middle of the road.
Petitioner stated that truck was running on the back side of the autorickshaw.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that he suddenly applied the brake, the truck might have collided with the autorickshaw.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that due to his negligence, accident taken place and accident has not taken place due to the negligence of the driver of the truck.
Petitioner stated that in the accident back side of the autorickshaw was damaged and as the truck dashed to the autorickshaw, he fell from the autorickshaw.
11. In the evidence, PW.2 Dr.Chidananda stated nothing regarding reason and mode of the accident.
12. As referred above, in this case, respondent No.2 Hemanth Kumar has produced incomplete evidence.

sentences.text: Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR and complaint pertaining to Cr.No.25/2021 registered by Wilson Garden police on 02.04.2021 at 14.00 hours, against the driver of Mahindra Truck bearing No.KA--51-AF-8110 regarding the accident taken place on 26.03.2021 at 9 a.m., between autorickshaw bearing No.KA-01-D-8582 and Mahindra Truck bearing No.KA-51-AF-8110, resulting in injuries to the petitioner on the basis of the complaint presented by the petitioner.
Ex.P.2 is the copy of the spot mahazar recorded on 02.04.2021.

Ex.P.3 is the copy of the sketch of place of accident wherein it is noted that on the middle of the junction of four roads, collision taken place between autorickshaw bearing No.KA-01-D-8582 and Mahindra Truck bearing No.KA-51-AF-8110,
which are running in the same direction.
Exs.P.4 & P.5 are the copy of the statement of Basavaraju S/o Ramaiah and Kiran S/o Jaganna recorded on 02.04.2021 by the Investigation Officer.

Ex.P.6 is the copy of the Motor Vehicle Accident report dated 05.04.2021.
14.

Ex.P.9 is the copy of the wound certificate dated 29.04.2021 in which reason for the injuries are noted as 'alleged history of RTA on 26.03.2021 at about 9 a.m., the patient while travelling in an autorickshaw, the vehicle hit against a tempo at Wilson Garden'.

Ex.P.10 is the copy of the chargesheet filed by Wilson Garden Traffic police in Cr.No.25/2021 against Chetan S/o Chandru - driver of the Mahindra Truck bearing No.KA-51-AF-8110 for having committed the offence punishable under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC.
15.
In this case, the evidence of eye-witnesses of the accident are not produced.

As referred above,
copy of the sketch confirms that on the middle of the junction of four roads, collision taken place between autorickshaw bearing No.KA-01-D-8582 and Mahindra Truck bearing No.KA-51- AF-8110,
which are running in the same direction.

Hence, I have concluded that on 26. 03.2021 at 9 am, in the junction of Wilson Garden main road and 4 th cross, due to the negligent use of the Auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-01- D-8582 by the petitioner and negligent use of Mahindra Truck bearing No.KA-51-AF-8110 by Chethan.S, at the ratio of 50:50, the accident taken place resulting in injuries to the petitioner.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 and 2 accordingly.

16. Issue No.4 : In the evidence petitioner stated that in the accident he ha suffered grievous bleeding injuries to his waist and other injuries, took treatment at Sanjay Gandhi Hospital,
Byrasandra, by spending Rs.1,00,000/-.
In the second page of Para-3 of the affidavit, petitioner stated that in the accident, suffered fracture of T12 Compression.
17. In the written statement, respondents No.1 & 2 denied the allegation regarding nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

In the cross- examination petitioner stated that he has suffered severe pain in back and immediately after the accident, shifted to Agadi Hospital, but no treatment was given at Agardi Hospital, then shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital,
wherein get treated conservatively for the period of one day.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that in the accident, he has suffered only simple injuries and never spent Rs.1,00,000/- for treatment.
Petitioner admitted non- production of documents regarding the income worth of Rs.30,000/- per month.
Petitioner stated that he has not surrendered the driving licence to RTO .

18. In the evidence PW.2 stated that on 15.06.2023 when clinically examined the petitioner, noticed that the petitioner suffered permanent physical disability in relation to spine which is at 15% to the Ahmed Jan T.A vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196465092/

sentences.text: whole body.

PW.2 stated that on 26.03.2022 (26.03.2021) petitioner when clinically examined,
noticed that in the accident, petitioner suffered T-12 wedge compression of vertebra.
In the cross- examination PW.2 admitted that he never treated the petitioner and admitted that petitioner never underwent surgery and explained that petitioner taken conservative treatment.

19. Wound certificate, Discharge Summary, X-ray, case file, medical bills and other medical records shows that in the accident, petitioner suffered Anterior wedge compression of D12 vertebral body with adjacent edema, subtle retropulsion causing mid anterior thecal sac identation, posterior disc bulge at D-3-4 level causing anterior thecal sac identation, diffuse disc bulge at L4-5 level causing anterior thecal sac identation and bilateral mild neural foraminal narrowing and mild degenerative spondylosis, took treatment at Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Byrasandra, by spending approximately Rs.4,344/-.
20.
In the Aadhaar Card marked at Ex.P.15, date of birth of the petitioner is noted as 15.03.1960.

As PW.2 Dr. Chidananda admitted that he never treated the petitioner and in the evidence PW.1 stated that he never surrendered his autorickshaw driving license to the RTO, I have inferred that the evidence of PW.2 is not sufficient to award compensation under the head of loss of future income (permanent functional disability).

Hence, Rs.50,000/- is assessed towards pain and suffering,
Rs.4.344/- towards treatment, Rs.10,000/- towards attendant, conveyance and nourishment charges, Rs.75,000/- (Rs.15,000 x 5 months) towards loss of income during treatment period and Rs.35,000/- towards loss of amenities and future happiness.
Hence, total compensation is assessed at Rs.1,74,344/- with current and future interest at 6% per annum.
21. In view of my findings recorded on Issue Nos.1 & 2, the petitioner is entitle to receive a sum of Rs.87,172/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a., as compensation.
Hence, I answer Issue No.4 partly in the Affirmative.
22. Issue No.3 :
In the written statement the respondent No.1/insurance company denied the subsistence of the policy with respect to Mahindra Truck bearing No.KA-51-AF-8110 as on the date of accident.
In the written statement, respondent No.2/owner of the Mahindra Truck bearing No.KA-51-AF-8110 submitted that as on the date of accident, the vehicle had insurance coverage with respondent No.1.

In the reply dated 07.04.2021 issued by the respondent No.2 to the notice issued under Sec.133 of IMV Act by the Investigation Officer marked at Ex.P.8, the respondent No.2 noted identification number of the policy issued by the respondent No.1 with respect to the Mahindra Truck bearing No.KA-51-AF-8110.
In this case, the respondent No.1/insurance company has not produced any evidence to show that the policy noted in the reply marked at Ex.P.8 is not concerned to the vehicle bearing No.KA-51-AF-8110.
Hence, I came to the conclusion that as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1/insurance company is the insurer of the Mahindra Truck bearing No.KA-51-AF-8110.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 is bound to indemnify the respondent No.2.

Hence, I answer Issue No.3 in the Affirmative and pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed by the petitioner under Sec.166 of IMV Act is partly allowed.
